subject.title: Add sms.read command and SMS as a messaging channel

question: Should OpenClaw support Android-device SMS ingress/reply as a first-class channel, and if so should it reuse the existing `sms` channel/config surface or use a separate Android-device plugin/channel boundary?
rationale: The remaining work crosses private Android SMS permissions, gateway node-event ingress, sender allowlists/pairing, outbound carrier-SMS authority, and the existing Twilio-owned `sms` channel namespace; automation cannot choose that product and security boundary safely.

options.title: Split command and channel decisions
options.body: Define a narrow dangerous/default-blocked Android `sms.read` command first, then separately design Android-device SMS ingress with fail-closed sender policy and a clear channel/config boundary.

options.title: Create a separate Android-device SMS channel
options.body: Use a distinct channel or plugin identity for connected-device SMS so it does not conflict with the existing Twilio-backed `sms` channel semantics.

options.title: Decline Android-device SMS ingress
options.body: Keep hosted Twilio SMS as the supported SMS channel and leave connected Android SMS limited to explicit node commands such as `sms.send` and `sms.search`.

recommendation.title: Split command and channel decisions
recommendation.body: Define a narrow dangerous/default-blocked Android `sms.read` command first, then separately design Android-device SMS ingress with fail-closed sender policy and a clear channel/config boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The most central unresolved boundary is coexistence with the current Twilio-backed `sms` channel and OpenClaw's plugin/core scope policy, tied to steipete's recent SMS channel work.
